text: Question: My SIM card shows 'No Service' after I inserted it in a new phone. Answer: ### Short Answer Reinsert the SIM, restart the device, and confirm the correct network mode (Auto) is selected. If the issue persists, the SIM's IMSI profile may need re-registration on the network — this is common after switching devices with an eSIM/physical SIM swap. Dial the SIM-status check code or visit a store for a replacement SIM with the same number. ### Detailed Explanation The suggested order matters: reinsert/restart/check-network-mode rules out simple device-side causes first, and only if those don't fix it does the explanation move to the network-side cause (IMSI profile needing re-registration), which specifically happens after a device switch involving an eSIM/physical SIM swap. ### Key Details | Detail | Value | |---|---| | Device-side checks | Reinsert SIM, restart device, confirm network mode is set to Auto | | Network-side cause | IMSI profile needing re-registration, common after device switch with eSIM/physical SIM swap | | If unresolved | Dial the SIM-status check code, or visit a store for a same-number replacement SIM | ### Troubleshooting | Symptom | Possible Cause | Diagnostic Check | Recommended Action | |---|---|---|---| | No Service' right after inserting SIM in new phone | Device hasn't picked up the network yet, or wrong network mode | Network mode setting (should be Auto) | Reinsert SIM, restart device, confirm Auto mode | | No Service' persists after reinsert/restart/mode check | IMSI profile not re-registered for the
